LADANG RANGKAIAN - FACT PACK (Far East Holdings Berhad, FEB group; near Merchong Mill, Pahang). Manager En. Mohd Khairul Nizam Bin Zakaria; Regional Senior Manager En. Musa Bin Abdul Halim; Assistant Manager En. Muhammad Alfan Fahmi Bin Ahmad Fauzi.

SOURCES. (1) PA Report 1/2026, visit 29 June 2026 by Planting Advisor En. Mohd Sufian Bin Yusoff; reviews Jan-May 2026 (May progress report). Previous PA visit 10 Dec 2025 (PA 2/2025, Jan-Nov 2025). (2) Agronomy Report 1/2026, visit 17 April 2026 by Senior Agronomist Mr. Lai Hong Heng; revised 2026 programme. Previous Agro visit 18 Nov 2025 (Agro 2/2025, set the 2026 programme). Earlier PA 1/2025 (17 Jun 2025) and Agro 1/2025 (20 Jun 2025).

AREA (PA, May 2026). Total 1,416.43 ha; all 1,392.50 ha mature, buildings 23.93 ha. Fields (ha, SPH): P12A 2012 161.40 (133), P13B 2013 141.80 (133), P13C 2013 301.20 (133), P13D 2013 243.30 (136), P14E 2014 202.80 (121), P14F 2014 232.20 (136), P14G 2014 109.80 (136). Agro census average 132 SPH (P14E 120 after elephant damage, Sep 2025); census last done Feb 2024. Palms prime, 12-14 years. Topography flat, 60% peatland per PA; Agro: 432.2 ha (31%) low-lying flood-prone and 165 ha (11.8%) peat; cambered bunds over 900 ha. Rainfall very high: 5-year average 4,800 mm over 145 days (PA); 4,821 mm, about 12 rain days a month, 33.5 mm per rain day (Agro).

PRODUCTION. Jan-May 2026: 9,116.16 t FFB vs budget 9,300.00 t and 8,932.09 t same period 2025; 6.55 t/ha vs budget 6.68 and 6.41 last year; annual budget 30,000 t (21.54 t/ha). CPO 1,734.62 t, OER 19.03%, KER 4.75%. 2025 full year 25,463.95 t, 18.29 t/ha, OER 18.69%. Full years: 2019 22,781.58 t (917.90 mature ha), 2020 26,176.26, 2021 27,345.67, 2022 27,134.22, 2023 24,863.15, 2024 25,997.77, 2025 25,463.95 t. Yield t/ha: 2020 18.80, 2021 19.64 (peak), 2022 19.49, 2023 17.87, 2024 18.67, 2025 18.29. 2025 monthly (t): Jan 1,882.62, Feb 1,548.53, Mar 1,696.33, Apr 1,934.01, May 1,870.60, Jun 1,740.47, Jul 2,048.75, Aug 2,433.10, Sep 2,651.93, Oct 2,742.61, Nov 2,726.27 (Jan-Nov 23,275.22 t, 14% below budget 27,150). Agro: main limiting factor is prolonged high water table and flooding in low-lying areas; flooded areas yield 12.91 t/ha vs 17.20 on higher ground (Jan-Oct 2025), bunch weight 12.14 vs 13.67 kg.

BLOCK YIELDS Jan-May 2026 (t, t/ha; PA Table 20): P12A 1,234.19 t 7.65; P13B 1,199.22 t 8.46; P13C 2,035.88 t 6.77; P13D 1,595.85 t 6.57; P14E 947.06 t 4.67; P14F 1,715.14 t 7.40; P14G 388.82 t 3.54. Jan-May 2025 (PA 1/2025): 6.27, 7.47, 5.54, 7.15, 5.45, 8.11, 4.29. Full-year 2025 vs 2024 (Agro): P12A 20.13 vs 18.53; P13B 21.36 vs 22.51; P13C 17.63 vs 17.23; P13D 18.94 vs 19.45; P14E 14.39 vs 15.16; P14F 22.41 vs 21.59; P14G 10.48 vs 16.5 (-36.5%, tapping-rights issue in G1 and G2). Jan-Mar 2026 vs 2025: estate 4.08 vs 3.68 (+11%); P14E -10% and P14G -19%.

HARVESTING. 55 harvesters vs 61 required (1:25 ha, slightly short); contractors DS Sinar (P12A, P13C, P14E; 34 vs 44), Rosmawati (P13B, P14G; 13 vs 17), Tangkas (P13D; 16 vs 15), Razmedin (P14F; 13 vs 13). Average interval 15 days, 10.00 rounds Jan-May 2026; 1.74 t per harvester-day (1.29 P14G to 2.69 P13B); rates RM38-45/t, earnings RM58.05-102.22/day. Machines: 3 Timac (475.50 ha, 12.84 t/machine-day, 2.75 t/harvester) and 5 Ginga EV (752.70 ha, 12.03 t, 2.59 t); mini crawlers replaced. Ripe crop above 90%, sent direct to mill. Agro Apr 2026: over-ripe 12% in P14F5 and 9% in P13C3, loose fruit collection improved, no rotten bunches; recommended frond-stacking started only in P13D3. Harvest & collection cost RM74.16/t vs RM77.03 budget.

COST (PA, Jan-May 2026, RM per t FFB): general charges 94.87 (budget 113.52); upkeep & cultivation 144.86 (173.60); harvest & collection 74.16 (77.03); total ex-estate 313.90 (364.15, -14%); annual budget 288.48. Per ha: general charges RM621.10 vs 758.14 (overspent upkeep labour quarters RM28.26/ha +109% incl. renting oil-mill quarters; MSPO RM7.63/ha +28% for signboards); upkeep RM948.35 vs 1,159.38: weeding 99.32, manuring 559.18 (-24%, late fertiliser), pests 42.08, drains 17.43, roads 111.81 (+8%), soil & water conservation 15.09, boundaries 51.83 (+119%, trench desilting), pruning 51.52. Jan-Nov 2025 cost was RM303.02/t vs RM277.66 budget. Capex 2026 RM345,784.10 of RM861,000 (tipping trailer RM20,500, Toyota Hilux RM145,197.70, Toyota Hiace school van RM159,586.40).

LABOUR (May 2026): 97 workers vs 107 required (1 per 14 ha): harvesting 55/61, driver-loader 9/9, weeding 9/13, manuring 16/14, mandors 3/3 and 5/7. In 5 months 5 recruited, 10 repatriated, 2 transferred out, 3 absconded.

MANURING. 2025 programme completed by Nov 2025 (Mix B 1,611.50 t, RP 339.40, kieserite 54.20 = 2,005.10 t). H1 2026 to May: 636.80 of 1,481.80 t (43%), delayed by late delivery; Jun GML 150.80 t not started. To Mar: 34% (NK2 delayed by late packaging at the mill). Wet store floor and spillage. PESTS. One round of rat baiting (STORM 1 bait/palm) over all 1,392.50 ha, done without a formal census; fresh damage still seen. 2025 census showed 24-75% fresh damage before baiting, 12-30% after. Barn owls 103 nests (1:14 ha), 89-90% occupied; boxes not cleaned yearly. No bagworm in 2026; 1,870 chains of predator plants. Elephants: damage escalated to toppled palms (P14E1, P13D3); 15 palms toppled in P13D/P14E; 4 km electric fencing (1.7 km Rangkaian, 1.3 km Sawak and Delima); damage reduced after fencing.

FIELD. Drains: 428 chains desilted in low-lying areas in 2026; 2,873.69 chains in 2025 plus bund lowering. Roads good: 3,190 chains graded (675 by estate mid-mounted grader), 90 chains lateriting in P13B, crusher run due in P13D. Mounding of 2,082 leaning palms in P13B and P14E. Thinning: 50 runt palms (P13C 15, P14E 35) in Mar 2026. Smallholder intrusion in P14G.

KEY ACTIONS. Speed up fertiliser delivery and application; rat census then systematic baiting; elephant fencing and patrols; palm census; reduce over-ripe bunches; adopt frond-stacking; targeted weeding, no strip spraying; drainage in low-lying blocks; EFB on high ground only; store hygiene; barn owl box cleaning; more harvesters; P14G security.

AGRONOMY OBSERVATIONS (Agro 1/2026). Two distinct palm groups: healthier palms on higher ground and stunted, yellowish, unproductive palms in low-lying flood-prone patches (P14F5, P14G3, P12A3, P14E1, P14E2) because of waterlogging and poor root aeration.
